messages:
cs-alyssa: Hey team — customer ACME (tenant acme-prod) reporting intermittent 502/504s against Hosted API (eu1) during large embeddings burst, started ~2024-11-02T15:20Z. Ticket #INC-12345. They attached a failing request + trace id, sending here for triage.

oncall-sam: Thanks, oncall is taking a look. Can you paste the sample request (headers + body size) and the trace id? Also confirm if streaming or non-streaming.

cs-alyssa: Trace: trace-id=abc123-def456. Non-streaming embedding request, single POST to /v1/embeddings, payload ~1.2MB (multiple inputs ~40). Headers: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `X-Tenant: acme-prod`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Customer says ~50 concurrent clients.

maria-eng-sre: Pulling edge logs for trace abc123-def456. Early evidence: Envoy shows upstream reset + 502s around the same window. Snippet from edge logs:
```
[2024-11-02T15:20:31Z] envoy [warning] upstream reset before response headers, code=CONNECT_FAILURE, trace=abc123-def456
[2024-11-02T15:20:32Z] nginx  [error]  recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while proxying
```
Also seeing auth-cache Redis latency spike (~200-400ms P95) at 15:20:30Z correlated with the 502 spike.

alex-runtime: Checked serving plane for that period — model workers OK, no OOMs. But we did see midfront keepalive pool saturation + queueing. Metrics: midfront keepalive_in_use=95/100, conn_waiters spiked. Pattern: large payloads + concurrency caused fanout to multiple upstreams and exhausted connection pool, then upstream resets. Repro note: run `ab` or k6 with payload ~1MB, concurrency 40-60 to reproduce.

oncall-sam: Good catches. So likely chain: auth latency delays request fanout -> midfront conns pile up -> upstream keepalive pool drained -> Envoy sees upstream close -> 502/504. Any quick mitigation we can try?

maria-eng-sre: Mitigation applied: reduced embed fanout for acme-prod to 1 and bumped midfront connection pool to allow higher ephemeral connections as temporary. Applied at 2024-11-02T15:28Z. Deploy log: `deploy-bot: route-change applied by oncall-sam at 1708888929`. After change errors dropped ~88% for that tenant in our metrics.

cs-alyssa: Customer confirmed dramatic improvement after you applied the routing change, thanks. They're ok with short-term routing to dedicated while we fix.

alex-runtime: Next steps from runtime side: add per-tenant fanout throttles and backpressure (limit concurrent embed shards), and add a soft circuit-breaker on upstream connection waits. From infra: investigate auth-cache Redis p95 spike — add local read replica for auth cache in eu1.

oncall-sam: I'll open a JIRA with action items: INFRA-789 (auth read-replica), RUNTIME-456 (per-tenant fanout controls), SRE-321 (lower keepalive timeouts + tune conn pool). Also add a playbook step to route-heavy tenants to dedicated if >X qps with large payloads.

maria-eng-sre: For triage notes: attach curl sample + headers (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'X-Tenant: acme-prod' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  --data-binary @large-embed-payload.json
```
Repro tip: use concurrency 40+, payload >800KB to hit the condition.

cs-alyssa: Updated ticket INC-12345 with mitigation, repro steps, and ETA for dedicated cutover. Customer wants postmortem once root cause is fixed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: routing-change applied for tenant=acme-prod by oncall-sam at 1708888929

oncall-sam: Closing the live escalation for now; will track the JIRAs and schedule a follow-up postmortem next week. If anyone sees a reappearance ping here.
